baseline_prompt_en: Photograph a vivid atompunk isotope orchard inside a decommissioned 1962 reactor greenhouse. Show one unmistakably adult woman, using the supplied portrait solely as appearance guidance for her long wavy dark hair, gently oval face, warm brown eyes, natural straight-to-softly-arched brows, and softly defined coral lips. She is a night-shift isotope horticulturist, calibrating a chrome seed-vault as cobalt-glass fruit pulses among waist-high hydroponic vines. Streamlined atomic-age machinery surrounds her: Bakelite controls, analog radiation gauges, finned aluminum housings, cream-and-turquoise enamel panels, a hanging bubble helmet, and orbiting-electron motifs. Her practical silver lamé coverall and clear acrylic dosimeter make her part of the worksite. Condensation beads on glass tubes while a compact analog robot offers a glowing specimen in articulated tongs. Prioritize credible hand-to-control contact, readable machinery, and a layered, lived-in retro-futurist environment. The result should feel like a physically built 1960s science-magazine production still: richly detailed, plausible, and unmistakably photographic.
